ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A bar magnet is placed on a horizontal tabletop. Above it, on the side near the right pole, a conducting rod perpendicular to it is suspended. In the figure, only the cross-sectional view of this rod is drawn, and it is marked that the current in this rod flows into the paper. The current in the conducting rod is gradually increased, and the magnet remains stationary throughout. The situation that may occur is (　 　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The frictional force on the magnet must increase

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A bar magnet is placed on a horizontal tabletop. Above it, on the side near the right pole, a conducting rod perpendicular to it is suspended (the direction of the current in the rod points into the paper). During the process in which the current in the conducting rod is gradually increased and the magnet always remains stationary, how does the frictional force on the magnet change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The frictional force on the magnet must increase
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, a bar magnet is drawn as a horizontal rectangle, placed on a horizontal tabletop indicated by diagonal-line shading; there is a vertical line in the middle of the magnet separating the left and right pole regions. Above the magnet, at a position偏 to the right, a circle with an “×” is drawn, representing the cross section of the conducting rod, and the “×” indicates that the direction of the current in the rod is perpendicular to the paper and inward. Then reason: The position of the conducting rod is fixed on the side above the right pole of the magnet, not at a left-right symmetric position, so the magnetic field produced by the bar magnet at that place has a definite magnitude and direction, and will make the conducting rod receive an Ampere force with a nonzero horizontal component. From F = I L × B, it can be known that when the magnetic field and the position of the conducting rod do not change, the magnitude of the horizontal component of the Ampere force is proportional to the current I; when the current is gradually increased, this horizontal component also gradually increases. According to interaction, the conducting rod exerts on the magnet a horizontal magnetic force equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. The problem states that the magnet remains stationary throughout, so the static frictional force of the tabletop on the magnet must balance this horizontal magnetic force; therefore, the magnitude of the frictional force on the magnet increases as the current increases.
